hook.en: Your family's savings in a bank can end up financing a metro line or a new factory. Financial markets are the bridge.

objectives.en: Define financial market and state its functions

narration.en: Your family's savings in a bank can end up financing a metro line or a new factory. Financial markets are the bridge.

body.en: A financial market is a market for the creation and exchange of financial assets. It links savers and investors by mobilising savings and channelling them into the most productive uses. Its functions are: mobilisation of savings, facilitating price discovery, providing liquidity to financial assets, and reducing the cost of transactions.
body.kn: ಹಣಕಾಸು ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಹಣಕಾಸು ಆಸ್ತಿಗಳ ಸೃಷ್ಟಿ ಮತ್ತು ವಿನಿಮಯದ ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ. ಉಳಿತಾಯ ಸಂಗ್ರಹ, ಬೆಲೆ ಅನ್ವೇಷಣೆ, ದ್ರವ್ಯತೆ ಒದಗಿಸುವುದು ಮತ್ತು ವಹಿವಾಟು ವೆಚ್ಚ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡುವುದು ಇದರ ಕಾರ್ಯಗಳು.

body.en: The money market deals in short-term funds with maturity up to one year. Its major participants are the RBI, commercial banks, non-banking finance companies, state governments, large companies and mutual funds. Instruments: Treasury bills, commercial paper, call money, certificates of deposit and commercial bills.
body.kn: ಹಣದ ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಒಂದು ವರ್ಷದವರೆಗಿನ ಅಲ್ಪಾವಧಿ ನಿಧಿಗಳ ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ. ಖಜಾನೆ ಹುಂಡಿ, ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಪತ್ರ, ಕರೆ ಹಣ, ಠೇವಣಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಣಪತ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಹುಂಡಿ ಇದರ ಸಾಧನಗಳು.

points.en: Treasury bill: issued by RBI for the Central Government; zero-coupon, issued at a discount, minimum ₹25,000
Commercial paper: unsecured promissory note of large companies, 15 days to 1 year; used for bridge financing
Call money: 1 to 15 days, mainly between banks; its rate is the call rate
Certificate of deposit: unsecured, negotiable, bearer form, issued by commercial banks and development financial institutions
Commercial bill: a trade bill accepted by a commercial bank

problem.en: A Treasury bill of face value ₹1,00,000 maturing in 364 days is issued at ₹94,000. What does the investor earn and why is it called zero-coupon?

steps.en: The investor pays ₹94,000 now and receives ₹1,00,000 at maturity.
Gain = 1,00,000 − 94,000 = ₹6,000, the difference between face value and issue price.
No separate interest (coupon) is paid; the return comes only from the discount.

answer.en: ₹6,000; it is zero-coupon because it is issued at a discount and redeemed at par with no interest payments.
